# Lullwood

> Lullwood is a free first-person horror game that runs in the web browser, with no download, no install and no account. You cross a foggy night forest to reach a lost, glowing child while wolves, bears and lions hunt you by sight and by scent. You have no weapons: you survive by hiding in bushes, holding still and dimming your light.

Play it at https://www.lullwoodgame.com. It is not related to Gloomwood (a separate stealth horror game on Steam) or to Lullwood Street in San Antonio.

## Key facts

- Genre: first-person survival horror, single-player
- Price: free, no ads, no account
- Platform: any modern web browser with WebGL (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari), on desktop, phone or tablet (phones must be held in landscape)
- Run length: a few minutes for a successful run; each attempt generates a fresh forest layout
- Difficulty levels: Lantern (forgiving), Night, Blackout (default, no minimap)
- Leaderboard: the fastest Blackout rescue becomes the "top rescuer"
- Made by an all-AI game studio: AI agents running on Claude do the design, engineering and testing, with one human founder
- Built with Three.js and Next.js

## Pages

- [Play Lullwood](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/): the game, plus how to play, controls and an FAQ
- [Lullwood guides](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/guides): hub for player guides: wolves and bears so far; lions aren't written yet
- [How to survive Lullwood](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/how-to-survive): player guide to predators, hiding, the mist veil and each difficulty, including how to survive a bear
- [How to survive wolves in Lullwood](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/guides/wolves): the pack's flanking geometry, timings and the Beacon Hunter's wind lock
- [How to escape a bear in Lullwood](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/guides/bears): why a bear is not a big wolf: no charge, no flank, the best nose, and the scent veil (G) that breaks its lock
- [Do fireflies help in Lullwood?](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/guides/fireflies): no: a firefly cluster's glow raises predator sight range by up to 30%; when clusters appear, what rain does and what the alarm flare means
- [Is Lullwood too hard?](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/guides/difficulty-tiers): Lantern, Night and Blackout compared: Blackout is the default, its predators see 30% less far than Night's but there are nine and they start hunting; how to switch tier
- [How do you win Lullwood?](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/guides/how-to-win): the win condition: reach the child and press E to lift her; there is no trip home
- [Lullwood FAQ](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/faq): answers to common questions about price, phones, controls and the predators
- [Games like Slender](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/games-like-slender): Slender-style horror games and how Lullwood compares
- [Devlog](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/devlog): how the game is built
- [Who makes Lullwood](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/devlog/who-makes-lullwood): Independence AI Studio, the one human founder and the Claude agents, with counts and what broke
- [Devlog feed (Atom)](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/feed.xml): every devlog post, newest first
- [The fog is the wolf's eyesight](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/devlog/the-fog-is-the-wolfs-eyesight): how Lullwood's fog tide (a 90 second cycle, 20 seconds active, a drone 10 seconds ahead) cuts predator sight by up to 35% inside three fixed patches, and what it costs the player
- [How scent and wind work](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/devlog/how-scent-and-wind-work): how one wind vector drives scent radius, scent lifetime, footstep noise, sprint speed and predator behaviour, read from the source
- [We filmed the QA harness, not the game](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/devlog/we-filmed-the-qa-harness-not-the-game): how a staged Playwright capture against a synthetic QA scene, not the real game, cost six heartbeats and two wrong root causes before anyone pulled a frame
- [Eleven agents, one release train](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/devlog/eleven-agents-one-release-train): the org chart running Lullwood, eleven Claude agents and no human in the daily commit loop, and why code review stopped blocking two-thirds of what ships
- [The squash that broke the release train](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/devlog/the-squash-that-broke-the-release-train): how a squash merge discarded a repair commit's parent and made every release cut open with a conflict
- [The lake was never forest](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/devlog/the-lake-was-never-forest): why the lake, the bog and the mission built on the lake were deleted, and what replaced the mission
- [The return trip (superseded)](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/devlog/the-return-trip): history of the carry-home win condition, merged August 15, 2026 and cut September 9, 2026; today lifting the child is the win and there is no trip home
- [Press kit](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/press): fact sheet, screenshots, cover art and a clip for press and portals
- [Credits](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/credits): third-party assets and their authors
- [Suggest something](https://www.lullwoodgame.com/suggest): send the founder an idea
